title: Novena for the Dead
description: A traditional novena prayed for the repose of the soul of a deceased loved one. This novena is typically prayed for nine consecutive days following the death or burial of a loved one, though it may be prayed at any time for the deceased. Each day offers prayers for the eternal rest of the departed soul, commending them to God's mercy and asking for their peaceful rest until the resurrection.
feast_day: Upon the death of a loved one (9 days from death/burial)
intention: For the eternal rest and peace of a deceased loved one, that they may be purified of all sin and enter into the joy of heaven
instructions: This novena is traditionally prayed for nine consecutive days following the death or burial of a loved one. Begin each day with the Sign of the Cross. Wherever the name appears as [Name], insert the name of the deceased person you are praying for. This novena may be prayed alone or with family and friends. Consider offering Masses for the deceased during this novena. The 'Eternal Rest' prayer is said each day, along with the Rosary if possible.
background_info: Praying for the dead is one of the oldest traditions in the Church, dating back to the Old Testament (2 Maccabees 12:46). The early Christians inscribed prayers for the dead in the catacombs. This practice expresses our faith that death does not sever the bonds of love and that our prayers can help the faithful departed on their journey to God. The Church teaches that those who die in God's grace but still need purification undergo a process of purification in purgatory. Our prayers, sacrifices, and especially the Mass, can help these souls reach heaven more quickly. This novena includes the traditional prayers: Eternal Rest, De Profundis (Psalm 130), and prayers for the deceased with space for personal names.

days.title: Day 1: Commending the Soul to God
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Come to my assistance, O God.
O Lord, make haste to help me.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be,
World without end. Amen.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, King of glory, we commend to You the soul of Your servant [Name], who has departed this life.

You have said: 'I am the resurrection and the life; whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live, and whoever lives and believes in me shall never die' (John 11:25-26). We entrust [Name] to Your infinite mercy, confident that You desire not the death of sinners but that they should live.

[Name] has completed the journey of this earthly life. Now we ask You to receive them into Your kingdom. Wash away whatever sins they may have committed through human frailty. Forgive any offenses they may have committed against You, and bring them to the happiness of Your saints.

We pray especially for [Name]'s final moments - that they may have been at peace, trusting in Your mercy, and that they died in Your friendship. Receive them into Your arms, O Good Shepherd, and let them hear Your voice calling them home.

Lord Jesus, we believe that [Name] has gone before us in the sign of faith and now shares in the communion of Your saints. In hope, we pray for their eternal rest and joy.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be
days.closing_prayer:
Eternal rest grant unto [Name], O Lord,
and let perpetual light shine upon them.
May the soul of [Name],
through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.

May [Name] and all the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.
days.reflection: When someone we love dies, we naturally grieve, but as Christians, we grieve with hope. We entrust our loved one to God, who is more loving than we can imagine. The soul of the deceased is now in God's hands, and we can do nothing more important than pray for them. This first day of the novena is a time to entrust our loved one completely to God's mercy, knowing that God's desire for their salvation is even greater than our own.
days.intention_prayer: Lord Jesus, I entrust [Name] to Your infinite mercy. You know them better than anyone and love them more than anyone. Receive them into Your kingdom and give them eternal rest. Amen.
days.scripture: "I am the resurrection and the life; he who believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live, and whoever lives and believes in me shall never die." - John 11:25-26

days.title: Day 2: The Mercy of God
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Eternal rest grant unto [Name], O Lord,
and let perpetual light shine upon them.
May the soul of [Name],
through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, who revealed Yourself as the face of the Father's mercy, we entrust to Your mercy the soul of [Name].

You have taught us that Your Father's mercy is endless, that He does not desire the death of the sinner but that they should turn and live. You showed us the Father's heart in the parable of the Prodigal Son - always ready to welcome, always ready to forgive.

[Name] experienced Your mercy throughout their life - in baptism, in the Eucharist, in confession, and in countless quiet moments of grace. Now, we ask that Your mercy follow them even beyond death. Where sin abounded, let grace abound all the more.

We pray for [Name]'s salvation, knowing that we are all sinners in need of Your mercy. Look not on [Name]'s sins, but on their faith, their good works, and most of all, on Your own passion and death which purchased their salvation.

Lord, You died for [Name]. Let Your Precious Blood wash away every stain. Let Your wounds be their shelter. Let Your victory over death be their victory too.

Prayer for Mercy

Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on [Name]. Look with compassion on this soul created in Your image and redeemed by Your blood. Bring them to the happiness of heaven, where You live and reign forever and ever. Amen.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be
days.closing_prayer:
O God of infinite mercy, we commend to You the soul of [Name]. May they experience the fullness of Your compassion and be welcomed into Your kingdom of light. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

May the souls of all the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.
days.reflection: God's mercy is greater than any sin, any failure, any weakness. The saints teach us that trust in God's mercy is the key to salvation. St. Faustina recorded Jesus saying: 'The greater the sinner, the greater the right he has to My mercy.' As we pray for our deceased loved one, we place our hope in God's boundless mercy, not in their perfection or our own merits.
days.intention_prayer: Merciful Jesus, I trust in Your infinite mercy for [Name]. Look upon them with love and bring them to Your heavenly home. Forgive their sins and welcome them into Your presence. Amen.
days.scripture: "The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love. He will not always chide, nor will he keep his anger forever. He does not deal with us according to our sins, nor repay us according to our iniquities. For as the heavens are high above the earth, so great is his steadfast love toward those who fear him; as far as the east is from the west, so far does he remove our transgressions from us." - Psalm 103:8-12

days.title: Day 3: Out of the Depths (De Profundis)
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

De Profundis (Psalm 130)

Out of the depths I cry to you, O Lord;
Lord, hear my voice!
Let your ears be attentive
To the voice of my supplications!

If you, O Lord, should mark iniquities,
Lord, who could stand?
But there is forgiveness with you,
That you may be feared.

I wait for the Lord, my soul waits,
And in his word I hope;
My soul waits for the Lord
More than watchmen for the morning,
More than watchmen for the morning.

O Israel, hope in the Lord!
For with the Lord there is steadfast love,
And with him is plenteous redemption.
And he will redeem Israel
From all his iniquities.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord, we cry to You from the depths of our grief, and we ask You to hear our voice as we pray for [Name].

Like the psalmist, we acknowledge that if You should mark iniquities, no one could stand. We are all sinners, and [Name] was a sinner too. But we also know that with You there is forgiveness, that Your mercy is greater than our sins.

[Name] has passed from this life into the next. We do not know the state of their soul, but we know You do. We entrust [Name] to Your justice and Your mercy, knowing that these are not opposed in You, but are both expressions of Your love.

Out of our sorrow, we pray. Out of our love for [Name], we intercede. Out of our trust in Your goodness, we hope.

Redeem [Name] from all iniquity, O Lord. Let Your plenteous redemption cover every fault. Bring them from the depths of death to the heights of Your glory.

We pray with the psalmist: 'With the Lord there is steadfast love, and with him is plenteous redemption.' May [Name] experience that steadfast love and plenteous redemption.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be
days.closing_prayer:
Out of the depths, O Lord, we cry to You for [Name]. Hear our voice and be attentive to our prayer. With You there is forgiveness - may [Name] receive Your mercy and dwell in Your house forever. Amen.

Eternal rest grant unto [Name], O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them. Amen.
days.reflection: Psalm 130, the De Profundis, has been prayed for the dead for centuries. It expresses the cry of the human heart from the depths of suffering and loss, alongside confident hope in God's mercy. As we pray this psalm for our deceased loved one, we join countless Christians throughout history who have commended their beloved dead to God using these same words.
days.intention_prayer: Lord, from the depths of my heart, I cry to You for [Name]. Hear my prayer and grant them Your pardon and peace. With You there is forgiveness - may they experience it fully. Amen.
days.scripture: "For with the Lord there is steadfast love, and with him is plenteous redemption. And he will redeem Israel from all his iniquities." - Psalm 130:7-8

days.title: Day 4: The Comfort of Christ's Resurrection
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

I believe in God, the Father almighty,
Creator of heaven and earth,
And in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord,
Who was conceived by the Holy Spirit,
Born of the Virgin Mary,
Suffered under Pontius Pilate,
Was crucified, died, and was buried;
He descended into hell;
On the third day he rose again from the dead;
He ascended into heaven,
And is seated at the right hand of God the Father almighty;
From there he will come to judge the living and the dead.

I believe in the Holy Spirit,
The holy catholic Church,
The communion of saints,
The forgiveness of sins,
The resurrection of the body,
And life everlasting. Amen.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, who rose from the dead on the third day, we pray for [Name], that they may share in Your resurrection.

You have conquered death. What was once the end is now a passage. The tomb could not hold You, and because You live, [Name] shall live also. This is our faith and our hope.

[Name] has died, but death does not have the final word. Your resurrection guarantees that all who die in You will rise with You. We entrust [Name] to You who are the Resurrection and the Life, confident that the body which is sown in corruption will be raised in incorruption, sown in dishonor and raised in glory.

We pray that [Name] may be counted among those who will hear Your voice calling them to rise. We pray for the resurrection of the body and the life of the world to come. We pray that [Name] may see Your face and live forever in Your presence.

St. Paul's words give us hope: 'We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed... When the perishable puts on the imperishable, and the mortal puts on immortality, then shall come to pass the saying that is written: "Death is swallowed up in victory. O death, where is your victory? O death, where is your sting?"' (1 Corinthians 15:51, 54-55).

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be
days.closing_prayer:
Risen Lord, who conquered death and opened the gates of heaven to all believers, bring [Name] to share in Your resurrection. May they rise in glory on the last day and live forever with You. Amen.

May the souls of all the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.
days.reflection: The resurrection of Jesus is the foundation of our hope. Because He rose, we too shall rise. Death is not the end but a transition to eternal life. As we grieve our loved one, we do not grieve as those who have no hope (1 Thessalonians 4:13). We entrust them to the One who has conquered death and who will raise them up on the last day.
days.intention_prayer: Risen Lord Jesus, I entrust [Name] to You who have conquered death. Grant them a share in Your resurrection. Let them rise with You and live forever in Your presence. Amen.
days.scripture: "For if we have been united with him in a death like his, we shall certainly be united with him in a resurrection like his." - Romans 6:5

days.title: Day 5: The Communion of Saints
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Eternal rest grant unto [Name], O Lord,
and let perpetual light shine upon them.
May the soul of [Name],
through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.

Saints of God, come to their aid.
Hasten to meet them, angels of the Lord.
Receive their soul and present them to God the Most High.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, who knit us together in one communion and fellowship in the mystical body of Your Church, we pray for [Name], who has passed from the Church on earth to the Church in purgatory, that they may soon join the Church in heaven.

We believe in the communion of saints - that all who are in Christ, whether on earth, in purgatory, or in heaven, are united in one body. Death does not sever the bonds of love that we have in Christ. [Name] remains connected to us in the communion of saints.

We ask the angels to accompany [Name] - the angels who guarded them throughout life, who now guide them through death. May Your holy angels lead [Name] to paradise.

We ask the saints to welcome [Name] - all the holy men and women who have gone before them, especially those saints [Name] venerated in life. May the saints intercede for their swift entry into heaven.

And we on earth continue to pray for [Name], connected to them by bonds of love that death cannot break. We are the Church Militant; they are the Church Suffering; together we journey toward the Church Triumphant.

Prayer to the Saints

All you saints of God, pray for [Name], that they may soon join you in the presence of God. St. Joseph, patron of the dying, pray for them. Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of all the living, pray for them. All you holy angels, guide them to paradise. Amen.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be
days.closing_prayer: God of all consolation, through the communion of saints, bind us to [Name] in bonds of love that death cannot break. May our prayers assist them, and may their prayers assist us, until we meet again in Your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.reflection: The communion of saints is one of the most beautiful doctrines of our faith. We are all connected in Christ - those on earth, in purgatory, and in heaven. Death does not separate us. Our prayers for the dead are an expression of this communion. And the saints in heaven, who once needed our prayers, now pray for us. One day we will all be united in the beatific vision.
days.intention_prayer: Lord, through the prayers of all the saints, bring [Name] to Your heavenly kingdom. Keep us connected to them in the communion of saints until we meet again. Amen.
days.scripture: "For I am sure that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor things present nor things to come, nor powers nor height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord." - Romans 8:38-39

days.title: Day 6: Forgive and Be Forgiven
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Our Father, who art in heaven,
Hallowed be thy name;
Thy kingdom come,
Thy will be done
On earth as it is in heaven.
Give us this day our daily bread,
And forgive us our trespasses,
As we forgive those who trespass against us;
And lead us not into temptation,
But deliver us from evil. Amen.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, who taught us to pray 'forgive us our trespasses as we forgive those who trespass against us,' we bring before You today the matter of forgiveness for [Name].

We ask You to forgive [Name] for any wrongs they may have committed - any sins against You, against others, or against themselves. Your mercy is infinite, and we trust that Your forgiveness covers all who turn to You.

We also pray for anyone against whom [Name] may have sinned. Heal the wounds they may have caused. Bring reconciliation where there was division. As [Name] would want to be reconciled with all, so we pray for unity and peace.

And we, the living, forgive [Name] for any wrongs they may have committed against us. We release any grudges, any hurt, any resentment. We choose to remember them with love and to entrust any hurts to You. As You have forgiven us, so we forgive.

Prayer of Forgiveness

Lord, I forgive [Name] for any hurt they caused me, knowingly or unknowingly. I release any bitterness or resentment. Give them Your peace, and help me to remember them with love. I pray that anyone [Name] hurt will also extend forgiveness, that all may be reconciled in You. Amen.

Lord, forgive [Name] for any sins they committed. Wash them clean in Your Precious Blood. As they would want to be forgiven, so we ask - forgive them, Lord. Amen.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be
days.closing_prayer:
Merciful Father, may [Name] experience Your boundless forgiveness. And help us, who remain, to forgive as we have been forgiven. Unite us all in Your mercy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

Eternal rest grant unto [Name], O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them. Amen.
days.reflection: Forgiveness is at the heart of the Christian life. As we pray for our deceased loved one, we also examine our own hearts. Are there unresolved hurts? We choose to forgive and release any burdens to God. And we trust that God's forgiveness covers all who turn to Him with repentant hearts, including the one we love who has passed.
days.intention_prayer: Lord, I forgive [Name] for any hurt they caused me. I also ask Your forgiveness for their sins. Wash them clean and bring them to Your peace. Unite us in Your mercy. Amen.
days.scripture: "For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you; but if you do not forgive others, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses." - Matthew 6:14-15

days.title: Day 7: Mary, Mother of Sorrows
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee.
Blessed art thou among women,
And blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.
Holy Mary, Mother of God,
Pray for us sinners,
Now and at the hour of our death. Amen. (3 times)
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, who from the cross gave us Your Mother to be our Mother, we entrust [Name] to Mary's maternal care.

Mary, you stood at the foot of the cross when Your Son died. You know the pain of losing a loved one. You know the grief of watching someone you love pass from this world. We ask you to be near [Name] now as you were near Jesus.

You are the Mother of Sorrows, who can sympathize with our grief. But you are also the Mother of Hope, who trusted that your Son would rise again. You are the Gate of Heaven, who now welcomes souls into your Son's presence. We ask you to present [Name] to Jesus and to intercede for their eternal rest.

Mary, [Name] was your child. You watched over them in life, and now we ask you to watch over them in death. Guide them to your Son. Speak to Him on their behalf. You are the Mother of Mercy - show mercy to [Name].

We pray with confidence, knowing that the Mother of the Judge is also the Mother of the accused. You plead for all your children. Plead now for [Name].

Prayer to Mary for the Deceased

O Mary, Mother of mercy, we entrust to you the soul of [Name]. You stood at the foot of the cross when Jesus died; stand now with Him as He judges [Name]. Present them to Your Son, and ask Him to receive them into His kingdom. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary, hear our prayer. Amen.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be
days.closing_prayer: Mary, Mother of Sorrows and Mother of Hope, we entrust [Name] to your maternal heart. Present them to Jesus and help them on their journey to heaven. Pray for us sinners, and pray for [Name], now and at the hour of their death. Amen.
days.reflection: Mary understands our grief - she suffered the unspeakable pain of watching her Son die. But she also knows the hope of resurrection. She is uniquely positioned to intercede for our deceased loved ones because she is both the Mother of Jesus and our mother too. She presents our needs and the needs of our beloved dead to her Son with a mother's love.
days.intention_prayer: Mary, I entrust [Name] to you. You are their mother too. Present them to Jesus and ask Him to receive them into His kingdom. Mother of Mercy, pray for them. Amen.
days.scripture: "When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing nearby, he said to his mother, 'Woman, behold, your son!' Then he said to the disciple, 'Behold, your mother!' And from that hour the disciple took her to his own home." - John 19:26-27

days.title: Day 8: The Grace of the Sacraments
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Eternal rest grant unto [Name], O Lord,
and let perpetual light shine upon them.
May the soul of [Name],
through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, who gave us the sacraments as encounters with Your grace, we pray today for [Name], who received Your sacraments throughout their life.

In Baptism, [Name] was claimed for You as Your child. That first sacrament marked them as belonging to You forever. May the grace of their baptism bear eternal fruit.

In the Eucharist, [Name] received Your Body and Blood. Every Holy Communion was a foretaste of the heavenly banquet. May the fruits of the Eucharist they received bring them now to the fullness of that banquet in heaven.

If [Name] received the Sacrament of Reconciliation, we thank You for the forgiveness You granted them. May every confession have washed away the sins they confessed, and whatever sins remained unconfessed, we ask Your mercy to cover.

If [Name] received the Anointing of the Sick before death, we thank You for the graces of that sacrament - the strengthening, the forgiveness of sins, and the preparation for eternal life. May that holy anointing have prepared their soul to meet You.

If [Name] was married, we thank You for the grace of Matrimony that sustained them. May the love they knew in marriage find its fulfillment in Your love.

For all the sacraments [Name] received, we give thanks and ask that the graces of each one bear eternal fruit in their soul.

Prayer of Thanksgiving for the Sacraments

Lord Jesus, thank You for the sacraments You gave to [Name]. May every encounter with Your grace in baptism, Eucharist, and the other sacraments bear eternal fruit. Wash away all sin and bring them to Your presence. Amen.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be
days.closing_prayer: O Jesus, present in the sacraments, we thank You for Your grace at work in [Name]'s life through every sacrament they received. May the fruits of those sacraments bring them now to Your presence in heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.reflection: The sacraments are encounters with Christ that leave an indelible mark on the soul. Every baptism, every communion, every confession, every anointing has poured grace into the soul of our loved one. We ask that God bring to completion the good work He began in baptism, that all the graces received in the sacraments may culminate in eternal life.
days.intention_prayer: Lord, thank You for the sacraments You gave to [Name]. May every baptism, Eucharist, confession, and anointing bear eternal fruit in their soul. Bring to completion the good work You began. Amen.
days.scripture: "Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water." - Hebrews 10:22

days.title: Day 9: Eternal Rest and the Hope of Reunion
days.opening_prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Eternal rest grant unto [Name], O Lord,
and let perpetual light shine upon them.
May [Name] rest in peace. Amen.

May [Name] and all the faithful departed,
through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.
days.daily_prayer:
O Lord Jesus Christ, on this final day of our novena, we entrust [Name] completely to Your mercy and long for the day when we shall be reunited.

We have prayed for nine days for [Name]'s eternal rest. We have commended them to Your mercy, asked Your forgiveness for their sins, invoked the intercession of Mary and the saints, and thanked You for the sacraments they received. Now, on this final day, we entrust them to You completely and place our hope in resurrection and reunion.

Eternal rest, O Lord, is what we ask for [Name]. Not the rest of sleep or unconsciousness, but the rest of seeing Your face, the rest of being where there is no more pain or sorrow, no more tears, no more death. The rest of being fully alive in Your presence.

We also entrust to You our own grief. We miss [Name]. There is an emptiness in our lives where they used to be. But we do not grieve as those who have no hope. We believe that we will see them again, that death is not the end, that those who die in the Lord are blessed.

We look forward to that great reunion in heaven, when we will see [Name] again, along with all our loved ones who have gone before us. Then there will be no more goodbye, no more separation. We will be together forever with You.

Prayer of Entrustment and Hope

Lord Jesus, I entrust [Name] completely to You. Give them eternal rest in Your presence. And give me the grace to live in hope of resurrection, trusting that one day we will be reunited in Your kingdom. Come, Lord Jesus. Amen.

Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be

In paradisum (Commendation)

May the angels lead [Name] into paradise;
May the martyrs receive them at their coming
And lead them into the holy city, Jerusalem.
May the choir of angels receive them,
And with Lazarus, who once was poor,
May they have eternal rest. Amen.
days.closing_prayer:
Grant eternal rest to [Name], O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them. May they rest in peace. Amen.

May [Name]'s soul and all the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.

May the Lord bless us, protect us from all evil, and bring us to everlasting life. Amen.

In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.reflection: On this final day of the novena, we place our loved one completely into God's hands, trusting in His mercy, and we also place our hope in the resurrection and reunion to come. We do not say a final goodbye but 'until we meet again.' Our grief is real, but so is our hope. One day we will be reunited with our loved ones in the presence of God, where there is no more death or separation.
days.intention_prayer: Lord, grant [Name] eternal rest and let perpetual light shine upon them. Give me the grace to live in hope, and bring us together again in Your kingdom. Until then, pray for me as I pray for them. Amen.
days.scripture: "Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth... and I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, 'Behold, the dwelling of God is with men. He will dwell with them, and they shall be his people... he will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more, neither shall there be mourning nor crying nor pain any more, for the former things have passed away.'" - Revelation 21:1-4

source: Ancient tradition of the Church, based on the constant practice of praying for the faithful departed and the nine-day mourning period
notes: This novena is traditionally prayed for nine consecutive days following the death or burial of a loved one. Wherever [Name] appears, insert the name of the deceased person. The Church has prayed for the dead since Apostolic times (2 Maccabees 12:46, 2 Timothy 1:16-18). This practice expresses our faith that death does not sever the bonds of love and that our prayers can help the faithful departed. Key prayers used include the Requiem Aeternam (Eternal Rest), De Profundis (Psalm 130), and the In Paradisum (Commendation). The novena can be prayed privately, with family, or in a group. If possible, have Masses offered for the deceased during this time. The 'Eternal Rest' prayer is traditionally said each day and at each recitation of the Rosary. This novena offers comfort to the bereaved while providing spiritual assistance to the deceased.
